papers.title: Low-Frequency Stable Single-Source Integral Equation
papers.abstract: Among the integral equations for scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects, single-source integral equations (SSIEs) provide the advantage of having only a single electric or magnetic current unknown. A well-conditioned SSIE can be obtained by appropriately combining the interior and exterior Calder\'on formulas. The condition number of the resulting operator appearing in the well-conditioned SSIE remains bounded at low frequencies. However, SSIEs still suffer from low-frequency cancellation, causing loss of significant digits in the solution, the right-hand side, and the system matrix. In this work, we apply a rescaling strategy based on quasi-Helmholtz projectors to the well-conditioned SSIE. Primal and dual space projectors are required since both primal and dual spaces are used to discretize the SSIE operators. We show that the solution of the rescaled SSIE is immune to catastrophic cancellations at low frequencies. Numerical experiments corroborate the method by testing the accuracy of the radiated field for extremely low frequencies.

papers.title: Accuracy and Efficiency of Lowest-order and Higher-Order Single-Source Integral Equations
papers.abstract: The single-source integral equation allows the modeling of the electromagnetic field by only tracking a single surface-supported current density. It features products of integral operators, which pose unique challenges for the modeler in both the discretization and solution of the equation. Due to the unique structure of the single-source equation, its conforming and stable discretization requires expanding one of the two physical traces in primal basis functions and the other in dual basis functions. Primal functions are expected to have better approximation properties than dual ones. In this work, we study the impact of this asymmetric representation on the accuracy of the solution and propose an approach from which both traces can be recovered using only primal functions with modest additional computational cost. Moreover, we propose an alternative discretization scheme based on approximating the inverse of the duality mapping induced by the surface normal cross-product operator through the quasi-Helmholtz decomposition. This discretization provides greater flexibility in the choice of function spaces, enabling both a higher-order extension of the single-source equation and a more efficient lowest-order discretization using only Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results show the impact of the representation in terms of primal and dual functions in both lowest- and higher-order discretization.

papers.title: Quantum-Inspired Tensor Train Spectral Solver for High-Resolution PDEs with Non-Periodic Boundary Conditions
papers.abstract: Tensor train (TT) methods enable high-resolution computational mechanics simulations by exploiting low-rank structure in discretized fields and operators. While the superfast Fourier transform (SFFT) has enabled efficient TT-based spectral solvers for periodic problems, corresponding representations for non-periodic boundary conditions remain underexplored. We introduce the superfast cosine and sine transforms (SFCT and SFST), extending the TT spectral framework to homogeneous Neumann and Dirichlet boundary conditions, respectively. Building on a quantum-circuit construction of the discrete cosine and sine transforms, we derive both transforms from a shared TT operator representation and prove that their TT ranks are bounded by $6r_S$, independently of the discretization order, where $r_S$ is the rank of the SFFT at the prescribed accuracy. The measured ranks plateau near 32 for grid sizes up to $2^{26}$ points. For Rayleigh-B\'enard convection, spectral pressure projection achieves up to a 7-fold speedup in the Poisson solve relative to a preconditioned physical-space TT solver while maintaining comparable accuracy. Three-dimensional computational homogenization achieves a 2-6-fold speedup and a 4-7-fold reduction in memory consumption compared with the existing TT-based approach. The results establish an efficient TT framework for spectral PDE solvers with non-periodic boundary conditions.

papers.title: The necessity of depth for artificial neural networks to approximate certain classes of smooth and bounded functions without the curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: In this article we study high-dimensional approximation capacities of shallow and deep artificial neural networks (ANNs) with the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation. In particular, it is a key contribution of this work to reveal that for all $a\in\mathbb{R}$, $b\in(a,\infty)$ with $\max\{\lvert a\rvert,\lvert b\rvert\}>1$ we have that the functions $[a,b]^d\ni x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^d x_i\in\mathbb{R}$ for $d\in\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ as well as the functions $[a,b]^d\ni x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\mapsto\sin(\prod_{i=1}^d x_i)\in\mathbb{R}$ for $d\in\mathbb{N}$ can neither be approximated without the curse of dimensionality by means of shallow ANNs nor insufficiently deep ANNs with ReLU activation but can be approximated without the curse of dimensionality by sufficiently deep ANNs with ReLU activation. More specifically, we prove that in the case of shallow ReLU ANNs or deep ReLU ANNs with a fixed number of hidden layers we have that the number of ANN parameters must grow at least exponentially in the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$ while in the case of deep ReLU ANNs with the number of hidden layers growing in the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$ we have that the number of scalar real parameters of the approximating ANNs grows at most polynomially in both the inverse of the prescribed approximation accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ and the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$, even if the absolute values of the ANN parameters are assumed to be uniformly bounded by $1$.

papers.title: On Approximate Computation of Critical Points
papers.abstract: We show that computing even coarse approximations of critical points is intractable for simple classes of nonconvex functions. We first present a family of $n$-variate cubic polynomials with coefficients in $\{-1,0,1\}$ that have exact critical points but for which no polynomial-time algorithm can write down a $\sqrt{n}/4$-approximate critical point in its standard representation. We then show that computational hardness persists when an exact critical point has a short representation. More specifically, we prove that for every fixed $\eta>0$, unless P $=$ NP, no polynomial-time (or even pseudo-polynomial-time) algorithm can take an $n$-variate cubic polynomial with rational coefficients ${c_\alpha}$ and return a point with gradient norm at most $(\max_\alpha |c_\alpha|)n^{1/2-\eta}$ whenever the polynomial has a critical point in $\{-1,0,1\}^n$. The algorithm may return an arbitrary point on all other inputs. Both results are essentially tight in their dependence on the dimension $n$. We also prove hardness results for lower-bounded functions and for an alternative notion of approximation, in which approximation is measured by distance to an exact critical point. Overall, our results stand in contrast to the commonly held belief that, in nonconvex optimization, approximate computation of critical points is a tractable task.

papers.title: A new angle on matrix-vector complexity
papers.abstract: The theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity has been useful for guiding the design of fast linear algebra algorithms. However, there is a large theory-practice gap in the study of *one-sided* methods, which use matrix-vector products with $\mathbf{A}$ but not $\mathbf{A}^\top$. In practice, for fundamental problems like solving linear systems, one-sided methods like GMRES are often the fastest. By contrast, worst-case analysis often shows pessimistic results, for instance showing that one-sided methods cannot solve a linear system with ideal condition number 1 unless they read the whole matrix $\mathbf{A}$. Such worst-case complexity results do not reflect real-world experience. To address this issue, this paper proposes a different theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity that includes information on the positioning of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ *in the complex plane*. Specifically, we characterize the "well-behavedness" of a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ through its *spectral condition number* $\kappa$ and its *angular eigenvalue gap $\theta$*, the angle of the largest sector not containing an eigenvalue. Under these parameters, we show that the one-sided complexity of the linear system problem is $\Theta(\theta^{-2}\kappa^{\pi/\theta})$. These results interpolate between known results for positive definite matrices ($\theta = 2\pi$), symmetric indefinite matrices ($\theta = \pi$), and general matrices ($\theta = 0$). This provides a rigorous explanation for the success of one-sided methods in practice, as it shows that one-sided methods beat the "optimal" two-sided algorithm (CGN) when the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ lie in less than half of the complex plane ($\theta > \pi$). Our analysis relies on tools from numerical analysis, complex analysis, and information-theoretic complexity, and the results are presented in a modular way to facilitate future use.

papers.title: Analysis and Optimal Approximation of Operator-Valued Riccati Equations with Unbounded Control Operators
papers.abstract: In this work, we present new results on the well-posedness and approximation of the operator-valued Riccati equations that arise in the context of control systems with unbounded control operators, e.g. interior point and boundary control systems. We first prove that the Bochner integral form of the operator-valued Riccati equation is well-posed even if the control operator is unbounded. We then leverage the favorable structure of the Bochner integral form to prove that the error of approximate solutions are bounded by the approximation error of the process $C_0$-semigroup. This general result then leads to the correct prediction of optimal error estimates for the finite element approximation of the Riccati equation. The analysis is carried out on both the time-dependent and stationary Riccati equations and our numerical convergence study on the weakly damped wave process and the thermal process with delta function actuation operators corroborate the results of our analysis.

papers.title: A decoupled BDF2-type integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert system in ferromagnetic multilayers
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete, linear, decoupled BDF2-type finite element integrator for the spin-diffusion Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert (SDLLG) system arising in spintronics. The SDLLG equations couple the magnetization dynamics with a diffusion equation for spin accumulation. The proposed numerical method combines a projection-free BDF2-type tangent-plane discretization of the magnetization dynamics with BDF2 time-stepping for the spin accumulation. By treating the coupling terms explicitly through extrapolation, each time step requires only two independent linear solves that can be performed in parallel. The analysis accommodates the usual exchange field and a general, possibly nonlinear, lower-order effective field. Unconditional weak convergence towards a global weak solution is shown. We also establish bounds on the deviation from the unit-length constraint. Under additional assumptions on the associated energy functional, an energy inequality for the limiting solution is obtained. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings.

papers.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
papers.abstract: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nystr\"om approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

papers.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
papers.abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $\delta^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.

papers.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.

papers.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
papers.abstract: The inf-sup constant $\beta(\Omega)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $\beta$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $\beta$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $\beta$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1\pi$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\le\beta\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\le\beta\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\le\beta\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $\beta$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $\beta^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $\beta$ had been available.

papers.title: Gradient-free MCMC exploiting low-dimensional Gaussian and nonGaussian posterior structure
papers.abstract: Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) for Bayesian inverse problems is expensive: the unknown is high-dimensional, every likelihood evaluation requires a forward solve, and gradients are often unavailable. The posterior typically differs from the prior in a few directions and is often approximately Gaussian in most of them but strongly non-Gaussian in a few. We propose the NQU sampler, a gradient-free MCMC method that splits the parameter space into non-Gaussian (N), approximately quadratic (Q) and uninformative (U) directions. The split is learned once, before sampling, from likelihood values, and each block is updated by a kernel suited to it; a collapsed update handles a global prior scale. Because the learned structure only shapes the proposals, every update leaves the exact posterior invariant, at the cost of one likelihood evaluation. We give a condition under which the blocks can be learned and show that, for likelihoods with exactly the learned structure, the spectral gap of the sampler does not depend on the dimension, whereas updating the scale given all coordinates can have a gap of order $1/d$. On the posterior axes, the NQU sampler, learning included, needed the fewest evaluations in four of five synthetic examples with $d=200$, among nine baselines including gradient-based ones; in those with non-Gaussian directions, gradient-free baselines needed at least ten times as many. On a methane ignition problem with 219 uncertain rate constants, it gave consistent estimates, whereas full-space robust adaptive Metropolis needed about 300 times as many evaluations and an ensemble sampler degenerated.

papers.title: Upwind finite element approximation of the gradient blow-up time for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation
papers.abstract: We analyze an upwind finite element method with piecewise linear elements for a viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation with a superquadratic gradient source term, subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. On polytopal inner approximations of smooth bounded domains in dimensions $N=1,2,3$, we prove maximum-norm convergence of the numerical solution to the exact solution before gradient blow-up and convergence of gradient-threshold times to the blow-up time under explicit mesh and regularity assumptions. We also verify the regularity assumption and finite-time gradient blow-up for an example on the disk, to which the main theorem therefore applies. Numerical experiments illustrate this gradient blow-up.

papers.title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics for Saddle Point Search under Continuous Symmetries
papers.abstract: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.

papers.title: A Unit-Gradient Neural Variational Method for Anisotropic Eikonal Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a variational neural method for computing viscosity solutions of the anisotropic eikonal equation. Building on the vanishing-viscosity principle, we minimize an energy functional whose Euler--Lagrange equation is the viscous anisotropic eikonal equation and introduce an auxiliary variable for the gradient, enforcing the constraint through a penalty. A key challenge in this formulation is to handle nonlinearity of the functional while controlling the interaction between the viscosity and penalty parameters. To address this challenge, we impose a unit-norm constraint on the auxiliary variable exactly, as prescribed by the eikonal equation. This removes the gradient from the exponentially weighted part of the functional and allows the viscosity and penalty limits to be studied separately. We establish two convergence results. First, for each fixed viscosity parameter $\epsilon>0$, we prove convergence to the viscosity solution as the penalty parameter $\lambda\rightarrow\infty$. Second, for the distance function to the boundary of a convex or smooth domain, we prove convergence as $\epsilon\rightarrow0$ for any fixed $\lambda>0$. The latter result motivates our stable numerical strategy, which keeps $\lambda$ fixed while decreasing $\epsilon$ whenever the training loss stagnates. The formulation is implemented using a neural network that satisfies the unit-norm constraint by construction and a mesh-free approach that evaluates the singularly scaled functional at randomly sampled points without requiring mesh refinement as $\epsilon\to0$. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method on diverse isotropic and anisotropic problems, including three-dimensional open-surface reconstruction from point clouds.

papers.title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
papers.abstract: Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML scheme with linear completeness. By using linear displacement field constraints to reconstruct the corresponding columns of the transition matrix, we ensure that the resulting numerical shape-function space contains the space of linear polynomials. We derive error estimates and establish convergence results of the improved scheme in the H1 and L2 norms. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate that the improved PIML achieves optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.

papers.title: Semi-Implicit Finite Volume Central Scheme for Hyperbolic Systems of Balance Laws with Adjustable Free Parameter approximation to relaxed source term
papers.abstract: This study develops a generalized framework for constructing a three-stage predictor-corrector finite volume scheme for solving hyperbolic balance laws with stiff relaxation source terms. The proposed scheme extends the central Nessyahu-Tadmor (NT) framework for the nonhomogeneous part of PDE and the integrals of the source terms are computed using an undetermined coefficient approach to introduce a free parameter \(\alpha\), which offers flexibility in formulation. A unified theoretical analysis is then carried out to characterize the properties of the resulting scheme and determine the admissible range of \(\alpha\). Specifically, uniform consistency and asymptotic properties are investigated along with $A$ -stability and $L$-stability, with the corresponding theoretical constraints combined to establish a common admissible range for the free parameter. The numerical performance of the scheme is subsequently evaluated through a sequence of test problems. Smooth-solution tests are used to assess its accuracy, while one-dimensional benchmark problems arising from different mathematical models are considered to examine its performance in comparison with existing numerical schemes. The assessment is further extended to ten two-dimensional Riemann problems to investigate the ability of the scheme to capture shocks and complex wave interactions along with computational cost.

papers.title: From Horner's rule to neural networks
papers.abstract: Horner's rule is usually taught as an efficient algorithm for evaluating a polynomial. Read as a recurrence, however, it is also a small computational graph: an input is propagated through intermediate states, while parameters enter locally. This note follows that elementary observation from polynomial evaluation to polynomial fitting. The equation $Va\simeq y$ then unifies least-squares approximation, interpolation and overparametrisation as different regimes of a fixed representation. Neural networks are introduced as the next step: the representation itself becomes parametrised and is learned from data. The purpose is pedagogical rather than encyclopaedic. It offers a numerical route into machine learning, using approximation, linear algebra and optimisation as familiar entry points.

papers.title: Computing expectations associated with McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations via probability-flow ordinary differential equations
papers.abstract: This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. The resulting mean-field ODE eliminates the need to approximate It\^{o} integrals and permits the use of higher-order integration schemes in time and stochastic space. However, simulating trajectories requires the score function of the MV-SDE's marginal law, which is approximated using a statistical estimator based on a system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional ODEs. The proposed estimator combines randomized quasi-MC in the stochastic variables and Runge--Kutta integrators in time, with efficient score estimation. Under assumptions on weak-error and variance convergence, the resulting estimator achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\text{TOL}^{-\left(\max\{\beta/\alpha,2\} + 1/\gamma \right)}\right)$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ denote, respectively, the weak-error and variance convergence rates with respect to $P$, and $\gamma$ is the order of the time-integration scheme.

papers.title: An adaptive finite element method for the interior problem of Helmholtz equations with generalized transmission boundary conditions
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new adaptive finite element method for solving the interior transmission problem with generalized transmission boundary conditions (GTBCs) involving a surface Laplace-Beltrami operator. A $\mathbb{T}$-coercivity technique relying on a lifting operator is established to show the well-posedness of the variational problem in appropriate nonstandard Sobolev spaces. Then both the a priori error estimates and a posteriori error estimates including the upper bound and local lower bound of the finite element discretization are constructed. Numerical examples are presented to illustrate the accuracy and convergence of the adaptive finite element method. Extension and high efficiency of the proposed method for the computation of the interior transmission eigenvalues for the problem with GTBCs are also discussed numerically.

papers.title: Toward Extreme-Scale Full-Wave Maxwell Simulation: Low-Dispersion Discretization and a Massively Parallel Three-Grid Solver
papers.abstract: Full-wave simulation of three-dimensional time-harmonic Maxwell problems over hundreds of wavelengths leads to indefinite systems with tens to hundreds of billions of unknowns. We present a matrix-free three-grid solver for such systems and its implementation on GPUs and CPUs. The solver is built on an interpolated optimized finite-difference (IOFD) discretization on the Yee grid, whose compact face and edge filters keep the phase error small at 6 points per wavelength, and it applies the same compact stencil on all three grids: an unshifted intermediate-grid correction is preconditioned by a complex-shifted auxiliary cycle, so that one preconditioner application performs a fixed number of stencil sweeps and reductions with storage linear in the number of unknowns. The implementation uses a partition nested across the grids, $s$-step smoothers that need one global reduction per smoothing call, and bfloat16 storage of the smoother bases. On 216 GPUs, complete solves with approximately $71.7$ billion complex unknowns take 77--504 seconds in homogeneous and heterogeneous media, with weak-scaling efficiencies of 89--91\% per preconditioner application; strong scaling reduces solves with 2.7 billion unknowns to 4.5--18 seconds on 64 GPUs. A CPU implementation reaches approximately $574$ billion unknowns on 13\,824 cores, and the computed fields agree with the outgoing Green field over domains of up to 956 wavelengths per direction.

papers.title: Bound-preserving Flux Limiters for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws on Two-Dimensional Adaptive Moving Meshes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bound-preserving finite-volume method on adaptive moving meshes for two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. The proposed method extends our previous one-dimensional framework [Y. Gu, G. Hu, and T. Tang, Adaptive mesh methods for hyperbolic conservation laws with bound-preserving flux limiters, arXiv:2602.12580] to two dimensions within the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework. The mesh velocity is determined by solving a moving mesh equation, allowing the numerical solution to evolve directly between consecutive time levels. A key challenge in this extension is to ensure compatibility between the evolution of the mesh geometry and the update of the numerical solution, as geometric information is essential to the convex decomposition underlying the bound-preserving construction in two dimensions. Specifically, the high-order scheme is reformulated as a convex combination of high-order sub-cell schemes, each of which is blended with its first-order counterpart to enforce the bound-preserving property. The discrete geometric conservation law ensures the compatibility needed to maintain this convex decomposition on moving meshes. The resulting correction acts locally at individual cell interfaces and is equivalent to applying a bound-preserving flux limiter, making the approach applicable to general unstructured or irregular meshes. The associated bound-preserving CFL conditions are established for both scalar conservation laws and the nonlinear Euler equations of gas dynamics. Extensive two-dimensional numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
papers.abstract: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.

papers.title: A Learning-Based Numerical Method for Biharmonic boundary value problems via the Almansi Decomposition
papers.abstract: We extend the learning-based numerical method (LbNM) to two-dimensional biharmonic boundary value problems, combining high accuracy with efficient repeated solves for different boundary data on a fixed domain. The method reconstructs a discrete boundary-to-solution operator from explicit biharmonic samples generated by the Almansi decomposition, using their boundary values and normal derivatives through Tikhonov regularization. Once constructed at prescribed evaluation points, the operator provides solutions for new boundary inputs by a single matrix-vector multiplication. Moreover, additional sample solutions can be incorporated through rank-one updates without rebuilding the operator. We establish a quantitative convergence estimate under a biharmonic continuation assumption. Numerical experiments on nonconvex domains demonstrate accuracy close to the double-precision limit for a smooth benchmark and high accuracy for solutions induced by nearby exterior singularities.

papers.title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $\Gamma$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.

papers.title: Higher Order Unfitted Discontinuous Galerkin Methods in Space and Time
papers.abstract: We present and analyse an unfitted space-time discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method of arbitrary order for convection-diffusion problems on moving domains in up to three space dimensions. The method is discontinuous in space and time and uses upwind fluxes, so that convection is stabilised without additional terms and a Ghost penalty is needed only in the vicinity of the moving boundary. We prove inf-sup stability in a problem-specific norm, which in addition to the coercive part controls the time derivative in the diffusion-dominated regime and the material derivative in the convection-dominated regime. From this we derive a priori error estimates of high order in space and time for both regimes, including vanishing diffusion. Numerical experiments confirm the convergence rates and the robustness with respect to the diffusion coefficient.

papers.title: An intrinsic kinematic wave model with conservative fluxes for overland flow on curved terrain
papers.abstract: Kinematic wave models, the simplest surface flow models, route overland flow by gravity alone and there is no pressure or inertial term to redistribute flow when the resulting velocities misroute it. Computed from piecewise-linear elevation data, this velocity jumps across the edges of the mesh: two neighboring cells can push water into each other, and the scheme can hold water in ponds that the terrain does not contain, or concentrate it where the data do not. We formulate the model intrinsically on the bed surface, with the depth normal to the bed as unknown, and obtain a single-valued edge velocity, in the unique edge frame of the intrinsic geometry, by correcting the raw cell field with the star-based conservative flux of Larson and Niklasson. Because the field is derived from data rather than from a Galerkin solution, the local problems are solvable only with a compatible load, the weak discrete divergence of the field being corrected, which for the slope is a discrete mean curvature of the terrain. With a Neumann boundary, every element is conservative, and the corrected field reproduces the cell average of the nodal divergence of the raw field, plus the divergence resolved inside the curved cells. Since any single-valued flux conserves mass, the correction is about consistency and robustness: the steady state of the upwind scheme solves an M-matrix system exactly when every cell drains to an outlet, and spurious ponds are closed classes of a transfer directed graph, computable before any simulation. Four rainfall tests, from a plane to a real catchment, are designed to verify the difference in storage and timing between the intrinsic and the classical form, the effect of the mesh on the consistency of the edge velocity, the robustness at a degenerate stationary point, and the application to terrain data.

papers.title: Three mixed-precision preconditioners for CholeskyQR
papers.abstract: CholeskyQR is an orthogonalization algorithm particularly well suited to modern computing architectures, but it may fail to produce numerically orthonormal columns when applied to ill-conditioned matrices. A customary solution is to first reduce the condition number of the input matrix by means of a preconditioner, and then apply CholeskyQR to the preconditioned matrix. We propose three mixed-precision techniques for constructing such preconditioners: mpSCQR, based on a shifted Cholesky factorization; mpEVDQR, based on the eigendecomposition; and mpLUCQR, based on a pivoted LU factorization. We prove bounds on the condition number of the matrix after mpSCQR, mpLUCQR, or a shifted variant of mpEVDQR has been applied. Our experiments compare the proposed preconditioners with existing deterministic and randomized alternatives. The results suggest that mpEVDQR and mpLUCQR can be substantially faster than traditional shiftedCholeskyQR, with mpLUCQR attaining performance comparable to that of the most efficient randomized preconditioners.

papers.title: Higher-Order Moments of Correlated Multivariate Hermite Polynomials
papers.abstract: Stochastic Galerkin methods reformulate a differential equation with uncertain parameters as a deterministic surrogate system by writing the solution as a series of polynomial basis functionals and projecting onto the parameter space. Given correlated Gaussian parameters, Rahman (2017) established solution convergence when the basis functionals are multivariate Hermite polynomials (MHPs), which is the setting considered here. Each term of the original equation contributes coefficients to the surrogate system, which we call the $N$th moments, that are expectations of products of the basis polynomials. Since the parameters are dependent, the $N$th moments do not factor into one-dimensional expectations via tensorization as they do in the independent case; consequently, their values are typically determined numerically at a nontrivial and compounding cost. Namely, the number of $N$th moments that emerge grows combinatorially with parameter dimension and truncation order. In this paper, we first relate MHPs and slowly growing functions --- which are smooth functions whose derivatives of all orders grow at most polynomially --- in correlated Gaussian parameters. In doing so, we derive an expression for the $N$th moment of an MHPs in terms of $(N-1)$th moments that can be evaluated exactly, along with sufficient conditions for the $N$th moment to vanish. Numerical examples illustrate the benefit of evaluating such moments directly without numerical approximation and confirm that formula-predicted values match sampling-based estimates.
